acceptance: Documented, tested way for parallel subagents to hold one claim each (distinct actors per subagent, or registered-batch mode), recorded in docs/agent/ and the todo skill's guidance for this repository.
A replaced MCP session of the same worker can re-adopt its own live claim with `take` (or the documented recovery is a single step), demonstrated once.
No change weakens the one-claim-per-worker rule for a single worker.
context:
DECISION GATE: changes to todo-db itself belong in the todo-db repository; this item covers the BenchBox-side configuration and guidance unless the owner directs otherwise.

2026-11-11: merged duplicate todo-db-parallel-batch-leaders-share-claim-slot-20261106 into this item. Batch-leader case: on 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-06 four batch leaders on one MCP server shared one worker identity, so a leader's take/prepare was refused while a sibling held a claim and audit records could not tell leaders apart. Options from that item: start each leader with its own TRACTABLE_ACTOR/--actor, or have tractable scope claims per batch owner generation; record the choice in docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md.
description: Observed repeatedly 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-01 while running tracker items in parallel subagents. All subagents share one todo-db worker identity, so only one can hold a claim: the others got E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS and worked unclaimed, finishing only after merge. When a subagent's MCP session was replaced mid-run, its `finish` returned E_CLAIM_STALE and `take` returned E_CONFLICT for a claim still held under the same identity, so the parent had to `takeover` to close sqlglot-fork-refresh-v30-26-0 and public-pseudonym-salt-automatic. The repository guide says separate servers with distinct --actor values are needed for concurrent workers, but the agent harness starts subagents on the parent's server.
